name: Saints Cyril and Methodius
dates: c. 826–869 and c. 815–885 · Thessalonica, Moravia and Rome
history: Two brothers from Thessalonica in Greece who carried the Gospel to the Slav peoples of central Europe. They devised an alphabet for the Slavonic language, translated the Scriptures and the liturgy into it, and won the Pope’s approval for worship in the people’s own tongue. In 1980 Saint John Paul II named them patrons of Europe alongside Saint Benedict.
life: Constantine, later called Cyril, was a brilliant scholar and teacher at Constantinople; his elder brother Methodius had been a governor before becoming a monk. In 863 Prince Rastislav of Moravia asked the emperor for teachers who could instruct his people in their own language, and the brothers were sent. Cyril created the Glagolitic alphabet, from which the later Cyrillic script, named in his honour, developed. Their use of Slavonic in the liturgy was attacked by Frankish clergy, so they went to Rome, where Pope Adrian II received them warmly and approved their books. Cyril became a monk there and died in 869; he is buried in the basilica of San Clemente. Methodius, consecrated archbishop, returned to the Slavs. He was imprisoned for over two years by bishops who opposed him, freed at the Pope’s command, and worked on until his death in 885. The Slav churches of East and West venerate them as their apostles.
prayerTo: Saints Cyril and Methodius, apostles of the Slavs, you gave the Gospel to a people in their own words and suffered for it with patience. Pray for Europe, that it may remember its Christian roots. Pray for the unity of East and West, for missionaries and translators, and for me, that I may speak of Christ in words others can understand. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the Christians of Eastern Europe and for unity between Catholics and Orthodox. Give to a charity that translates or distributes the Scriptures.
meditation: The brothers believed every people should be able to praise God in its own tongue. How could you speak of your faith in words your neighbours would understand?
